title: What If Every Human Disappeared Right Now?

analysis_notes.thumbnail_vs_video_mismatch: Thumbnail is a thick-outline cartoon golden retriever before/after; the video itself is flat-vector infographic animation with stick figures. Dogs get only ~25 s of screen time (2:50-3:02, 6:32-6:40).

title_pattern.notes: Classic universal-premise 'What If' with two amplifiers: 'Every Human' (total scale, includes the viewer) and 'Right Now' (present tense, makes it about the viewer's current moment; the hook literally opens with 'Right now'). No number or superlative; the payoff list (planes fall, subway floods, reactors) is held back for the hook. Evergreen topic (cf. Life After People) refreshed with a deep-time timeline structure ending in a billion years.

thumbnail.composition: Pure white background split into two equal halves, no divider line. Left: happy golden retriever head-and-chest, tongue out, red collar with gold tag. Right: same dog feral: matted fur with leaves and twigs, red eyes, bared fangs, scar, torn collar. Each dog fills ~80% of its half's height; label text above each.
thumbnail.text: 'TODAY' (left) and '50 YEARS LATER' (right), black heavy rounded comic-style all caps across the top. Only 4 words in total.
thumbnail.colours: White ground, golden-yellow fur, black thick outlines, red collar as the only accent. Very high contrast and readable small; stands out against dark space/earth thumbnails in the same niche.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: No scale contrast: it is a before/after (state) contrast of the same subject at the same size, the visual equivalent of the time-jump premise. Cute vs. menacing emotional flip.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Pets are the most personal stake in an 'everyone vanishes' scenario: viewers immediately ask 'what happens to MY dog?'. The before/after split communicates the time-jump idea without needing the title, triggers curiosity and mild threat, and is legible at mobile size. It sells one emotional moment of the video rather than its actual art style (clickbait-adjacent but the topic is covered).
thumbnail.copyable_recipe: Two-panel TODAY / N YEARS LATER of one relatable subject (pet, house, your street) on white, thick outlines, 3-4 words of label text, one red accent.

hook.verbatim_first_5s: Right now, there are about 10,000 planes in the sky. More than a million people, 35,000 feet above the ground.
hook.verbatim_to_snap: Right now, there are about 10,000 planes in the sky. More than a million people, 35,000 feet above the ground. Now watch what happens when I snap my fingers. Every person on Earth is gone. No war, no virus, no bodies, just gone.
hook.device: Present-tense concrete statistic ('Right now ... 10,000 planes') that puts the viewer in the real world this second, then a magic trigger ('watch what happens when I snap my fingers') with an on-screen vanish. Then rules-of-the-game in a triad ('No war, no virus, no bodies'), eerie continuity details (coffee still hot, cars still rolling, planes on autopilot), and a rapid escalating preview of three payoffs with timestamps ('In a few hours ... In two days ... In about a week, a countdown ends at more than 400 nuclear reactors'). Ends on an open loop ('the last trace of the human race ... isn't even on this planet') paid off at 9:44-10:41, and an explicit start signal 'Let's start the clock.'
hook.visual_device: Plane cabin cross-section with stick-figure passengers who blink out on the snap; big stat callouts (10,000 / 1,000,000+) on a dark world map; countdown timer ticking on a night map; clock face at 00:00:00 that launches the persistent HUD.
open_loops: Planes fall in a few hours (paid 1:14)
NYC subway underwater in two days (paid 2:19)
Countdown at 400+ reactors (paid 3:22, explicitly: 'this is the countdown from the start of the video')
Last trace of humanity is not on this planet (paid 9:44 moon, 10:13 Voyager)

beats.summary: Right-now stat (10,000 planes, 1M people airborne), snap of the fingers, everyone vanishes.
No war, no virus, no bodies. Coffee still hot, cars rolling, planes on autopilot with nobody inside.
Rapid preview of payoffs with deadlines (planes fall, subway floods in 2 days, 400+ reactor countdown) plus the 'last trace isn't on this planet' mystery; 'Let's start the clock.'
1B+ cars lose drivers, highway chain crashes, engines idle and die, first silence in millennia.
Planes run out of fuel, glide down over oceans, forests, cities. 'Nobody hears them land.'
Power plants need people, safety shutdowns cascade like dominoes; Earth's night lights vanish by end of day one; wind farms and hydro dams hang on; tease 'a much bigger problem has started ticking'.
NYC subway pumps 13M gallons a day; no power, no pumps, tunnels full in ~36 h; London, Tokyo, Paris drown from below.
Hundreds of millions of pets waiting by the door; farms with 20B chickens and 1B cattle; some gates were open and animals walk out.

Explicit callback to the opening countdown. Reactors scrammed fine; spent fuel pools need circulation; diesel backup lasts one week; pools heat, boil, dry; fires spread radiation at many plants: 'worst nuclear disaster in history, and nobody left to call it one'.
'Here's the strange part': for nature it's survivable. Chernobyl preview: expected dead zone, got wolves, lynx, bison, horses. Radiation is less dangerous to animals than we are.
Fires with no fire department burn neighborhoods for weeks; first winter freeze-thaw splits cracks; seeds; grass through highways, weeds in Times Square. 'We're only getting started. Let's speed up.'
'Your home' gets a roof hole, rain, rot, mold; 'the house you live in right now' collapses around year 50.
'Look up': satellites without ground control decay and burn up; ISS among the first; 'the greatest light show in history' watched by nothing that understands it.
Losers: cockroaches, rats, head lice. Winners: forests, fish, whales in quiet water. Pets: small dogs die, big dogs form packs, 'Cats are fine. Cats were always fine.' (comic relief)
Bridges survive only via constant painting; bare steel rusts, cables snap; Golden Gate and Brooklyn Bridge fall into their rivers.

Towers, dams, 'things built to last forever': skyscraper = steel skeleton wearing glass, collapses ~year 300; NYC becomes forest with square hills, Dubai under sand, Amsterdam/New Orleans underwater; dams fail, wall of water, rivers return to old paths.

'What's still standing? Not the newest, the oldest.' Pyramids, Great Wall, temples, Roman roads, tunnels; Mount Rushmore erodes 1 inch per 10,000 years, recognizable for ~7M years. Re-hook: 'something else lasts even longer than stone, and it's a lot less impressive.'
Air recovered (CO2 ~100k years); no surface trace; dig down to 'our line', a hand-thick rock layer of concrete, glass, metal, plastic: 'everything we ever fought over'.

'But I told you ... it's up there.' Moon footprints from 1969 still sharp for millions of years, six landing sites, family photo; then Voyager's golden record (55 languages, music, a child laughing) built to last a billion years: 'a child's laugh will still be traveling between the stars'.
'Let's go back to that snap.' Timeline recap: lights out in a day, cities flooded in a week, homes 50 years, towers 300, forgotten after 1,000.

Everything permanent stands only because somebody maintains it; callbacks to painters, pumps, control room. 'The world we built isn't a thing. It's a job.' Earth doesn't need us; what makes it ours lasts as long as we keep showing up.
Comment prompt tied to theme (one building, one object, one message to survive a million years), 'I really want to read these', subscribe ('you're clearly curious ... it's free').

pacing.speech_coverage: voice runs 0:00-12:03 with no music-only gaps longer than ~2 s; short punchy sentences (avg ~6.7 words per whisper segment, 266 segments)
pacing.shot_notes: ~120 distinct scene setups over 726 s (avg ~6 s). Frame-diff at 2 s sampling flags a significant visual change every ~4.3 s (167 changes) because most setups animate internally (counters, water rising, figures vanishing). Hard cuts are rare (scene-detect 0.25 finds ~58, many in bursts); transitions are mostly crossfades, whooshes into time-jump titles and match-continuity (same street/cabin/globe reused).
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~30-45 s: each timeline stop opens with a time stamp ('Three hours in', 'Day two', 'Day three is the hard one', 'Day seven', '100 years') and most close with a forward tease ('a much bigger problem has just started ticking', 'we're only getting started', 'something else lasts even longer than stone').
pacing.time_allocation: First week (0:51-4:15) gets ~28% of runtime; year 1 to 1,000 years ~36%; 1M+ years and space ~13%; recap/thesis/CTA ~12%. Front-loads the fast, concrete, high-stakes events and accelerates through deep time ('Let's speed up').

techniques_worth_copying: Persistent HUD: top-left odometer 'DAY 2 / SINCE THE SNAP' (starts as HH:MM:SS clock e.g. 03:00:01, then DAY n, then YEAR n with comma formatting) plus a bottom timeline scrubber with labelled stops NOW, 10 SEC, 3 HRS, DAY 1, DAY 2, DAY 3, DAY 7, 1 YR, 10 YRS, 50, 100, 300, 1,000, 10,000, 1M, 1B that lights up as the video advances. Gives constant progress feedback and a reason to keep watching to the end of the bar.
'Right now' + snap trigger: open on a real present-tense statistic, then a single magic action that starts the scenario, shown as figures blinking out.
Preview payoffs with deadlines in the hook, then explicitly cash them in ('this is the countdown from the start of the video'). Countdown timer on screen is a literal ticking clock.
Mystery open loop held to the last 15% ('the last trace ... isn't even on this planet'), paid with an emotional image (a child's laugh between the stars).
Personalisation shots: 'your home', 'the house you live in right now', pets waiting by the door. The scenario is aimed at the viewer's own life.

Mechanism mini-explainers built from simple cutaways (subway pump, spent-fuel pool, freeze-thaw crack, rusting bridge cable): one cause-effect chain, 3-5 one-word captions ('IT FREEZES / IT EXPANDS / WIDER').
Staccato triads in VO and on-screen text ('No war, no virus, no bodies'; 'Rain gets in. Wood rots. Mold eats the walls.'; 'Concrete cracks, gates jam, water finds a way').
Same-scene state change: one illustration (house, skyscraper, Pripyat, street) re-shown at successive ages so decay reads instantly without new assets.
Comic relief and list format mid-video (winners vs losers; 'Cats are fine. Cats were always fine.') to reset attention around the 6-minute mark.
Big-number counters that roll (1,000,000,000+, 19,947,329,662+, 6,999,937 YEARS FROM NOW, 996,498,450 YEARS).

Circular structure: 'Let's go back to that snap', recap timeline with icons, then reverse earlier shots (lights back on, operators back at posts) to deliver the thesis 'The world we built isn't a thing. It's a job.'
Thematic comment CTA (choose one thing to survive a million years) with a mock comment box and an animated subscribe button.

code_only_remake.feasibility: Very high. Everything is flat 2D vector: no textures beyond subtle gradients/grain, no lip sync, minimal character animation. One of the most Remotion-friendly references in the library.
code_only_remake.art_style: Flat infographic vector with muted palette: navy/slate night scenes (#0f1726-ish), steel-blue building blocks with window grids, warm sunset gradients, cyan UI accents, orange/yellow highlight text. Condensed geometric sans (DIN-like) in tracked all caps for labels. Thin film-grain/vignette overlay.
components_needed: HUD: elapsed counter (HH:MM:SS clock, then DAY n, then YEAR n; comma formatting; ease-out roll) with small 'SINCE THE SNAP' subtitle and cyan left bar + bottom timeline scrubber with labelled stops and progress glow, driven by storyboard time-stamps
Stick-figure character: circle head with big eyes, line body, 3-4 poses (idle, point, look up), plus crowd generator with random colored shirts; fade/blink-out vanish effect
Procedural skyline generator (rects with window grids, parallax layers, lights-on/off per window with staggered timing)

World map + globe: SVG world map (Natural Earth/topojson) with glowing dot layers (flights, cities, reactors), label pins, zoom to region; orthographic globe via d3-geo with night-lights dots that fade
Countdown timer DD:HH:MM:SS and big rolling number counters
Cross-section diagram kit: soil strata, tunnel capsule, pool with rods, thermometer, gauge, water level fill, bubbles/steam particles
State-change assets: house (intact, roof hole, mold, overgrown, collapsed), skyscraper (glass, skeleton, rust, dust collapse), bridge (cables snap), dam (cracks, burst)
Vegetation overlay (grass/vines/trees growing via scale/clip reveal) and simple animal silhouettes (dog, cat, cow, wolf, deer, whale, fish school, rats, cockroach, owl)
Weather/particles: rain, snow, fire (flicker shapes), smoke puffs, meteors with trails, light rays underwater
Space scenes: starfield, moon surface with craters and footprints, Voyager probe icon, golden record disc, solar system orbit rings
Split-screen and triptych panel transitions; balance-scale metaphor; LOSERS/WINNERS split; icon recap timeline
Kinetic text: stacked word reveals, big time-jump titles with whoosh-in scale, small tracked caption labels
UI mocks: comment box with typing cursor, subscribe button click state
code_only_remake.audio: Calm male documentary VO (~146 wpm) via Kokoro/Piper; low ambient pad music; whooshes on time jumps; snap SFX; light ticking on countdowns.
code_only_remake.effort_estimate: Hardest pieces are the globe/map layers and the many unique scene props (~60 setups). Building the HUD + skyline + stick figure + map kit first covers ~40% of shots; state-change assets cover another ~25%.
